docRequirement: headless.md:88 (a <Note> inside the "Pipe data through Claude" section) binds non-interactive stdin intake to a hard ceiling: "As of Claude Code v2.1.128, piped stdin is capped at 10MB. If you exceed the cap, Claude Code exits with a clear error and a non-zero status. To work with larger inputs, write the content to a file and reference the file path in your prompt instead of piping it." Three obligations: a 10MB cap on the piped stdin the process reads (headless.md:77 — "Non-interactive mode reads stdin, so you can pipe data in"), a CLEAR ERROR on breach, and a NON-ZERO exit status. The workaround sentence is advice, not a fourth obligation, but it is the text the error message should point at.
current: `readPrompt` (apps/cli/src/index.ts:423-442) is the fork's only piped-stdin intake and it is unbounded. It enters the stdin branch when `--stdin` is present or there is no positional message and `process.stdin.isTTY` is false (:426-428), then declares `const chunks: string[] = []` (:429), takes `Bun.stdin.stream().getReader()` (:430) and loops `while (true) { const { done, value } = await reader.read(); if (done) break; chunks.push(decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })) }` (:432-436) before `chunks.join('')` (:437). There is no byte counter, no comparison, no throw and no `process.exit` anywhere in the function; `grep -an 'MAX_\|_LIMIT\|BYTES' apps/cli/src/index.ts` returns zero hits, so the file holds no size constant of any kind. Both callers are affected and neither adds a check: `cmdSend` (:576) and `cmdRun` (:766, this fork's headless `claude -p` analogue — it spawns its own server with `printMode: true` at :783 → `spawnLocalServer` sets `PRINT_MODE_ENV_VAR` at :620), each validating only `!message.trim()` (:577, :767). A binary-safe `grep -ran 'Bun.stdin|process.stdin' apps/cli/src` hits exactly two lines, :427 and :430 — there is no second stdin reader, and no `--input-format` exists (`grep -an 'inputFormat|input-format' apps/cli/src/index.ts` finds none; `stream-json` appears only as an OUTPUT format at :457 and :2048), so `readPrompt` is the whole surface. No layer below supplies the cap: the text travels `sessions:sendMessage` over the WsRpcServer, and all three `new WebSocketServer(...)` sites (packages/server-core/src/transport/server.ts:294, :310, :325-328) pass no `maxPayload`, so the only backstop is the `ws` default of 100 MiB — ten times the documented limit, and it surfaces as a connection close, not a clear error. `grep -ran maxPayload` over packages/server-core/src, packages/server/src and apps/cli/src returns zero hits. The fork actively ships and documents the capped surface: docs/cli.md:121-125 shows `echo ... | nessy-general-agent send <id>` and `cat document.txt | ... --stdin`, docs/cli.md:196-199 shows `cat error.log | nessy-general-agent run "..."`, and neither mentions a size limit. The nearest same-named constants are a SIBLING subsystem and do not apply: `MAX_STDIN_DATA_BYTES` (1 MiB) and `MAX_STDIN_WRITE_BYTES` (64 KiB) in packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:120-129, :487 bound what the host WRITES to a child process's stdin, not what the CLI reads from its own.
divergence: The entire cap is absent — not a wrong constant, not a wrong key name, and not enforcement one layer up. All three of the page's obligations are missing together: no byte accounting (so no cap), therefore no clear error and no non-zero exit on breach. Two shape details the fix must get right, because getting either wrong would satisfy the letter and miss the point. (1) The cap must be measured on RAW BYTES read from the pipe (`value.byteLength`), not on the decoded string's `.length` — a UTF-8 multibyte payload would otherwise pass a character-count check well past 10MB. (2) It must fail FAST, cancelling the reader the moment the running total crosses the ceiling, not after the loop drains: the current code holds every chunk in `chunks` and then joins, so peak memory is roughly twice the input, and a post-hoc length check would still let a multi-gigabyte pipe exhaust memory before the error could be printed — which is the failure the cap exists to prevent. Separately, the error must reach the user as a clear message on BOTH paths: a throw from `cmdSend` is already caught by main()'s handler (apps/cli/src/index.ts:2242-2245 → `err(msg)` + `process.exit(1)`), but `run` is dispatched at :2132, BEFORE that `try` opens at :2184, so a throw out of `cmdRun` escapes main() entirely as an unhandled rejection instead of the documented clear error.

change.what: Add `export const MAX_PIPED_STDIN_BYTES = 10 * 1024 * 1024` immediately above `readPrompt`, with a comment citing headless.md:88. Inside the stdin branch, keep a `let bytes = 0`; after each successful `read()`, do `bytes += value.byteLength` and, when `bytes > MAX_PIPED_STDIN_BYTES`, `await reader.cancel()` and `throw new Error('Piped input exceeds the 10MB stdin limit. Write the content to a file and reference the file path in your prompt instead of piping it.')` BEFORE pushing the chunk — the cancel-then-throw ordering is what keeps peak memory bounded. Also append `chunks.push(decoder.decode())` after the loop to flush the streaming decoder (today a trailing incomplete multibyte sequence is silently dropped). Change the signature to `export async function readPrompt(words: string[], restArgs?: string[], stdinStream: ReadableStream<Uint8Array> = Bun.stdin.stream())` and read from `stdinStream.getReader()` at :430 — that default-parameter injection is the only test seam available, since the function is currently module-private and codegraph reports no covering tests. Do NOT call `process.exit` inside `readPrompt`; throwing keeps it unit-testable and matches how the schema gate already reports (:583-588).

Wrap the `await readPrompt(args.rest, args.rest)` call at :766 in a `try { ... } catch (e) { err(e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)); process.exit(1) }`, byte-for-byte the shape of the schema gate four lines below it (:774-780). Required, not cosmetic: `run` is dispatched at :2132, outside main()'s `try` (:2184), so without this the throw leaves main() as an unhandled rejection and the user gets a stack trace rather than the documented clear error. `cmdSend` (:576) needs no change — main()'s catch at :2242-2245 already turns the throw into `Error: <msg>` on stderr plus `process.exit(1)`.

change.symbol: new `describe('readPrompt stdin cap')` beside the existing `parseArgs` block
change.what: Two cases, using the injected stream (`new ReadableStream({ start(c) { c.enqueue(new Uint8Array(n)); c.close() } })`) and importing `readPrompt, MAX_PIPED_STDIN_BYTES` from './index.ts' alongside the existing `parseArgs` import: (1) positive — a payload of exactly `MAX_PIPED_STDIN_BYTES` bytes resolves and the returned string has the expected length, proving the boundary is inclusive; (2) negative — `MAX_PIPED_STDIN_BYTES + 1` bytes delivered as two chunks rejects with a message containing '10MB', asserted via `expect(readPrompt([], ['--stdin'], stream)).rejects.toThrow(/10MB/)`. A third cheap case is worth it: enqueue a chunk far over the cap and assert the stream's `cancel` was observed (a `cancel()` spy on the ReadableStream source), which is what proves fail-fast rather than drain-then-check.

One sentence after each block stating that piped stdin is capped at 10MB and that a larger input exits non-zero with an error, pointing at the write-to-a-file workaround. The fork's own CLI reference currently documents the piping surface with no limit, so it would otherwise contradict the new behaviour.

blastRadius: Small and contained, with one boundary to name explicitly. Direct readers: `readPrompt` has exactly two callers, `cmdSend` (apps/cli/src/index.ts:576) and `cmdRun` (:766), both in the same file; codegraph reports no covering tests for any of the three, so the tests above are new coverage rather than edits to existing assertions. Exporting `readPrompt` and `MAX_PIPED_STDIN_BYTES` widens apps/cli/src/index.ts's public surface, which is already the test entry point (apps/cli/src/commands.test.ts imports `parseArgs`, `resolveApiKey`, `shouldSetupLlmConnection` from it). Gates: `cd apps/cli && bun run typecheck` and `bun test apps/cli/src/` — note AGENTS.md's trap that `bun run typecheck:all` does NOT cover apps/cli, so the root typecheck proves nothing here. Wire/persistence: this change does NOT cross either. It rejects input before `client.invoke('sessions:sendMessage', ...)` (via sendAndStream at :549/:551), so no envelope, RPC signature or stored session shape changes, and no server-side handler is touched. The adjacent hardening that WOULD cross the wire is deliberately excluded: setting `maxPayload` on the three `new WebSocketServer(...)` sites (packages/server-core/src/transport/server.ts:294, :310, :325-328) would change frame acceptance for every RPC client — the Electron main process, apps/cli, and any external consumer — and is a risk trigger under AGENTS.md's Implementation-First budget. Do not fold it into this fix. Also untouched by design: `MAX_STDIN_DATA_BYTES`/`MAX_STDIN_WRITE_BYTES` and their tests (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/process-supervisor.ts:120-129, :487; process-supervisor.test.ts:181-183, :1214) belong to the child-process supervisor and must keep their current values.
userImpact: Observable, but only with a large pipe. `cat big.log | nessy-general-agent run "what is failing?"` — the exact form docs/cli.md:196-199 recommends — is accepted at any size with no warning. At tens of MB the run appears to succeed while the whole file is joined into one prompt string, so the user's real experience is a silently exhausted context window and a truncated or confused answer, with no message telling them the input was too big. Push it further and the failure mode becomes wrong rather than merely quiet: peak CLI memory is roughly twice the input (every chunk retained in `chunks` before `join`), so a multi-hundred-MB pipe ends in a Bun allocation failure or an OOM kill; and once the serialized text frame passes the `ws` 100 MiB default the connection is closed mid-send, which surfaces to the user as `Error: Send timeout — no completion event received` from sendAndStream (:562) — a transport timeout, not "piped stdin is capped at 10MB". So today the user gets, in order of input size: silent context exhaustion, then a misleading timeout, then a crash — never the documented clear error. The same holds for `send` with `--stdin` (docs/cli.md:124).
notes: Files read for every line cited: apps/cli/src/index.ts (230-260, 418-442, 569-594, 750-830, 2112-2135, tail, plus grep-confirmed line indexes for :2184 `try` and :2242 `catch`), packages/server-core/src/transport/server.ts (285-340), docs/cli.md (110-135, 188-205), apps/cli/src/commands.test.ts (head, for the import shape), apps/cli/package.json and root package.json (gate commands). Absence claims all made with binary-safe `grep -ran`: `Bun.stdin|process.stdin` across apps/cli/src (2 hits, both in readPrompt), `maxPayload` across packages/server-core/src + packages/server/src + apps/cli/src (0 hits), `MAX_|_LIMIT|BYTES` in apps/cli/src/index.ts (0 hits), `inputFormat|input-format` in apps/cli/src/index.ts (0 hits). Two things I did not execute and would verify at implementation time. (1) The page writes "10MB" without units, so 10 * 1024 * 1024 versus 10_000_000 is a guess; I chose MiB because that is the prevailing convention in this repo's own limits (process-supervisor.ts uses 1 MiB / 64 KiB) and because the difference is 4.6% at a ceiling that exists to prevent an OOM, not to be exact. If a future doc revision or an observed Claude Code error string pins the decimal value, change the constant only. (2) I did not run a large pipe against the built CLI, so the ordering of the three degradation modes in userImpact (context exhaustion → ws close surfacing as the :562 timeout → allocation failure) is derived from reading the code paths, not measured; the specific claim that an unhandled rejection out of cmdRun still exits non-zero under Bun is likewise inferred from Bun's default unhandled-rejection behaviour and is the weakest link in the cmdRun argument — but it does not affect the fix, since the try/catch is needed for the 'clear error' half regardless. Deliberately out of scope, adjacent findings on the same page: headless.md:91 (an unreadable stdin should print a stderr warning and CONTINUE with the command-line prompt — the fork has no such handling either, but that is a different obligation), and headless.md:160 (the 30-second output-drain wait on exit).
